current.title: Piranesi
current.author: Susanna Clarke
current.blurb: A man lives alone in a house of endless halls and tidal seas, keeping careful notes on the statues and the birds. It is a puzzle, but the pleasure of it is the voice — patient, decent, entirely unbothered by the fact that his world makes no sense. Bring your theories; we will disagree warmly.
questions: Does the House work better as a place or as a metaphor — and does it matter?
Piranesi is kind almost to a fault. Is that innocence, or damage?
Where did the ending leave you: relieved, or a bit bereft?

events.title: March meeting — Piranesi
events.note: Soup, because it is still March. Bring a passage you marked and one thing that annoyed you.

events.title: Bookshop crawl
events.note: Four shops, one pub, a strict twenty-pound ceiling that nobody observes.

events.title: April meeting — winner of the vote
events.note: Whichever of the four nominees takes it. Marek has promised the good coffee.

events.title: Klara and the Sun
events.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
events.note: Priya’s, Barnsbury. Split the room — half moved by the ending, half unconvinced Klara was ever really looking.

events.title: Cold Enough for Snow
events.author: Jessica Au
events.note: The Alma, back room. Short enough that everyone finished it.

events.title: A Christmas Memory
events.author: Truman Capote
events.note: Jonah’s, Angel. Christmas cheese; read the last pages aloud.

events.title: The Overstory
events.author: Richard Powers
events.note: Ruth’s, Canonbury. Long. Two people skipped to the trees.

events.title: Dept. of Speculation

events.note: Argued about whether the fragments earn their whiteness. They do.

events.title: Concrete: A Life

events.note: Nobody’s favourite, but a good night.

events.title: The Remains of the Day
events.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
events.note: The high point of the year so far — unanimous.

events.title: H is for Hawk
